1. Read what the StingRay is.

## What it is

- The **StingRay** came out in **1976**, from Music Man, founded by ex-Fender employees; Leo Fender co-designed it with Tom Walker (Wikipedia, "Music Man StingRay").
- Walker designed its **active preamp**, powered by a **9-volt battery** (Wikipedia).
- One large **humbucker**, placed nearer the bridge than a Precision's pickup, its two coils wired **in parallel** (Wikipedia).
- Early StingRays had a **2-band EQ** (bass and treble); later a **mid** control was added (Wikipedia). This page has both: **StingRay (2-band)** and **StingRay (3-band)**.

## Its sound

- A **passive** tone knob can only take treble away. An **active** EQ is an amplifier inside the bass: it can **boost** as well as cut.
- The preamp also buffers the pickup, so the cable does not dull it: a bright, clear sound.
- Coils in parallel have less inductance than in series: brighter than most humbuckers.
- Near the bridge: a punchy, thin-ish attack, good for slap. Chic's "Le Freak" used its "low-end thump" (Wikipedia).
- On this page each EQ knob runs 0-10 with **5 = flat**, about 15 dB of boost or cut at the ends, bass at 80 Hz, treble from 2.5 kHz, mid at 500 Hz. These numbers are this site's guesses (unverified).

## The controls

The StingRay's control area, drawn after the real one (positions approximate). Drag a knob (or use the arrow keys), then press a ▶ button. The sound is this site's physical model of a plucked bass string through these pickups and this wiring, into an amp; nobody has compared it with a real bass. The picture under the buttons shows the harmonics of the open A string (55 Hz) at the jack (bars) and the circuit alone (line).

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="stingray" data-set="{}" data-play="riff"><p><b>EQ flat (5 and 5).</b> Bright and clear.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="stingray" data-set="{&quot;bass&quot;:8}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Bass up to 8.</b> More thump: a boost no passive bass can make.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="stingray" data-set="{&quot;treble&quot;:8}" data-play="lead"><p><b>Treble up to 8.</b> More click and snap, a slap kind of sound.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="stingray" data-set="{&quot;bass&quot;:8,&quot;treble&quot;:8}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Both up.</b> The "smile" EQ: lows and highs up, mids left behind.</p></div>
<div class="bs-step" data-bass="stingray" data-set="{&quot;treble&quot;:1}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Treble down to 1.</b> Dark and round, closer to an old P-Bass.</p></div>
```
